title: New crate: a generic node graph widget in pure egui (nodes, wires, pan and zoom, layered layout)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
The maintainer asked for this issue on 2026-11-15 and set its priority to `P?` (paused):

> Lets create an issue for creating that crate.. [...] Put both as P?

His question before that: "could we make an egui-graph crate ourselfs for this?"

What is wanted: a small crate of our own (working name `crates/egui-graph`) that draws a node graph with `egui` only. It knows nothing of CAM.

Scope:
- Nodes with a title, an icon slot, a status colour and ports.
- Wires between ports, drawn as curves with `egui::Painter`.
- Pan and zoom. Selection of one node or a box of nodes.
- A layered automatic layout, left to right, from the edges of the graph.
- The host gives a plain graph snapshot each frame. The widget returns events (node clicked, node moved, wire dragged from A to B). The widget changes no host data.
- Step 1 is read-only (paint, layout, pan, zoom, select). Step 2 adds the edit gestures (drag a wire, move a node, keyboard).

Rules that apply:
- The crate depends on `egui` only. It adds no third-party node-graph dependency (`egui-snarl`, `egui_graphs` were considered and not chosen: they bind us to their `egui` version).
- The edge from `camcraft-ui` to the new crate needs a `docs/decisions/` entry in the same PR (AGENTS.md "No new dependency between our crates without a decision").
- No source file is longer than about 400 lines.
- The crate builds on Windows, Linux, macOS and the browser build.
- The crate has its own tests with the egui test harness. They do not start CamCraft.
- Each edit that the host makes from a widget event is an undoable command (AGENTS.md "Everything Is a Command").

Estimate: step 1 is `effort:medium`, step 1 and step 2 together are `effort:high`.

Done means: the crate is in the workspace with its tests, a demo graph renders with pan, zoom, selection and automatic layout, and the widget returns its events to the host.
